subject: general
question: Cells were first observed in cork by ______ in 1665.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Hooke:**

 
 
• **Robert Hooke** was an** English scientist in the 17th century who is often credited with first observing cells.**
 
• He used a **microscope** to observe the structure of **a thin cutting of cork **and noticed it was made up of **tiny, hollow compartments which he called "cells" because they reminded him of the cells of a monastery.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theophrastus:**

 
 
• Known as the** "Father of Botany,"** Theophrastus was a Greek philosopher who studied under Plato and Aristotle.
 
• He is credited with major contributions to botany and biology, but he lived in the 4th century BC, well before the discovery of cells.
 
 
 
• **Edward Jenner:**
 
 
• Edward Jenner was an **English physician** and scientist who was the pioneer of smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
 
• While his work was instrumental in the field of immunology, he was not involved in the initial discovery of cells.
 
 
 
• **Anton van Leeuwenhoek:**
 
 
• Anton van Leeuwenhoek, a **Dutch scientist from the 17th century,** is considered the "Father of Microbiology."
 
• He greatly improved the microscope and was the first to document the existence of **bacteria, protists, sperm cells, and blood cells.**
 
• While he did significant work with microscopic observations, he did not first observe cells in cork - that was Hooke.
